sources.entry: Coder - Remote development machines on your own infrastructure. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker/K8S/deb

summary.one_liner: Coder is a self-hosted platform for cloud development environments and AI coding agents, running on your own infrastructure.
summary.what_it_does: Coder lets you define cloud development workspaces in Terraform, such as EC2 VMs, Kubernetes Pods, or Docker containers, and connect to them through a WireGuard-based tunnel. Idle workspaces can be shut down automatically to save costs. Coder Agents runs an AI coding agent whose loop executes in the control plane on your infrastructure, so no API keys are placed in workspaces. The README says it supports bringing your own model (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock, or self-hosted) and provides centralized model governance, cost tracking, and audit logging. Install is via a shell script on Linux and macOS or a binary/installer from GitHub Releases on Windows, and `coder server` starts a server with a built-in database by default; PostgreSQL 13+ is recommended for production.
use_cases: Provision reproducible developer workspaces from Terraform templates
Onboard new developers quickly into a standard dev environment
Auto-shutdown idle cloud dev machines to cut costs
Run AI coding agents on your own infrastructure without sharing API keys
Centralize AI model access, auditing, and cost tracking for a dev team
Connect VS Code or JetBrains to remote workspaces
notable: Workspaces defined as Terraform templates, targeting VMs, Kubernetes pods, or Docker containers
Coder Agents runs AI coding agent loops in the control plane so no LLM credentials live in workspaces
Built-in database and automatic *.try.coder.app access URL for quick evaluation
Official integrations include VS Code and JetBrains Toolbox extensions, a Terraform provider for coderd, and a Coder Registry
Idle workspace auto-shutdown for cost control
caveats: Dedicated support and some features are part of paid Coder Premium
Production setup needs an external PostgreSQL database and access URL, plus sizing per the validated architecture guides
